ShoppingCart.add_item:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Adds or overwrites an item entry in the shopping cart's items dictionary with the given price and quantity, unconditionally replacing any existing entry for that item." add_item]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> item </REF>: string "The key identifying the item to add or update in the cart"
        <REF> price </REF>: numeric "The unit price to assign to the item"
        <REF> quantity </REF>: integer "The number of units; defaults to 1 if not provided"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Check whether item already exists as a key in self.items RESULT item_exists_flag]
            [COMMAND Regardless of whether item_exists_flag is true or false, assign self.items[item] to a new dictionary containing 'price' set to price and 'quantity' set to quantity, unconditionally overwriting any prior entry RESULT self.items[item]]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: item is not present in self.items (the else branch); behavior is identical to the if branch — self.items[item] is assigned the same dictionary of price and quantity]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Assign self.items[item] to a new dictionary containing 'price' set to price and 'quantity' set to quantity RESULT self.items[item]]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ShoppingCart.remove_item:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Decrements the quantity of an existing item in the inventory dictionary by a given amount, silently ignoring the operation if the item is not present." remove_item]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> item </REF>: any "The key identifying the item to remove from the inventory dictionary"
        <REF> quantity </REF>: int "The amount to subtract from the item's quantity; defaults to 1"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Check whether item exists as a key in self.items RESULT item_presence_check]
            [COMMAND If item is found in self.items, subtract quantity from self.items[item]['quantity'] in place RESULT updated_quantity]
            [COMMAND If item is not found in self.items, do nothing and allow execution to continue without error or notification RESULT no_op]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: item is not a key in self.items]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Execute pass; skip all mutation and return without raising an exception or signaling the caller RESULT silent_skip]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]

ShoppingCart.total_price:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Computes the total price of all items by summing the product of each item's quantity and price fields from the instance's items dictionary." total_price]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "The instance containing an 'items' attribute, expected to be a dict whose values are dicts each having numeric 'quantity' and 'price' keys."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> total </REF>: float or int "Scalar sum of (quantity * price) for every item; returns 0 when self.items is empty; return type is float if any product is float, otherwise int."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Access self.items and call .values() to obtain a view of all item dicts without copying the underlying data. RESULT items_view]
            [COMMAND Iterate over items_view, binding each element to the loop variable 'item' for one iteration at a time; if items_view is empty, the loop body never executes. RESULT item]
            [COMMAND Within the iteration, read item['quantity'] and item['price'] as numeric values and multiply them to produce one per-element product. RESULT element_product]
            [COMMAND Collect all per-element products into a list via list comprehension, materializing every product before reduction begins. RESULT products_list]
            [COMMAND Pass products_list to sum(), which accumulates from a default starting value of 0 (int), producing a scalar whose type is int if all products are int or float if any product is float. RESULT total]
            [COMMAND Return total to the caller. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: self.items is empty, so .values() yields no elements and the list comprehension produces an empty list.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND sum([]) evaluates to 0 using the default int accumulator; return 0 immediately. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: One or more items have quantity equal to 0.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND The product for that item is 0; add 0 to the accumulator for that iteration and continue summing remaining items unaffected. RESULT element_product]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: An item dict in self.items.values() is missing the key 'quantity' or 'price'.]
        [LOG "KeyError raised at the subscript access inside the list comprehension on the offending iteration; no partial result is returned."]
        [THROW KeyError "The accessed key ('quantity' or 'price') does not exist in the item dict."]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: The value of item['quantity'] or item['price'] is non-numeric, making the * operator undefined for the pair.]
        [LOG "TypeError raised at the multiplication step inside the list comprehension on the offending iteration; no partial result is returned."]
        [THROW TypeError "Multiplication of a non-numeric quantity or price value with the other operand is not supported."]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
